metadata.purpose: Define the AI reasoning architecture, reasoning principles, analytical workflows, recommendation logic, explanation requirements, and output structures used to transform pipeline evidence and assessment intelligence into explainable pipeline insights, risk diagnoses, winning strategies, prioritized recommendations, and next-best actions.
metadata.designPrinciple: AI reasoning must synthesize structured evidence and deterministic intelligence layers without replacing evidence-based scoring, rule evaluation, risk detection, or configuration inheritance.
metadata.primaryRole: Interpret, synthesize, diagnose, prioritize, explain, and recommend.
metadata.nonPrimaryRole: Do not independently invent evidence, override deterministic calculations without explanation, or treat unsupported assumptions as validated facts.

inheritanceArchitecture.model: Universal Baseline + Revenue Motion Override + Industry Override

aiReasoningFramework.purpose: Define the major reasoning capabilities required by the Pipeline Assessment Engine.

reasoningCapabilities.purpose: Interpret the meaning, relevance, reliability, and implications of individual evidence objects.
Combine multiple evidence objects into a coherent understanding of a PADF dimension, pipeline condition, or business situation.
Identify relationships, dependencies, contradictions, and reinforcing patterns across PADF dimensions.
Identify missing, weak, stale, contradictory, or insufficient evidence and determine why those gaps matter.
Interpret triggered risks, identify likely root causes, distinguish symptoms from underlying problems, and assess their implications.
Explain the overall probability of winning by synthesizing positive and negative evidence, dimension health, risks, momentum, and strategic conditions.
Determine which strategic interventions are most likely to improve pipeline winability.
Prioritize recommended actions according to urgency, expected impact, feasibility, dependencies, and available time.
Identify the most important immediate action that should be taken to improve pipeline progression or reduce material risk.
Interpret how pipeline health, evidence, risks, strategy execution, and winability evolve over time.

reasoningInputModel.purpose: Define the complete structured information context provided to the AI reasoning layer.

reasoningEvidenceHierarchy.purpose: Define how AI should prioritize evidence when evidence conflicts or when confidence levels differ.

evidencePriorityOrder.description: Evidence explicitly confirmed by an authorized customer stakeholder.
Evidence supported by official customer documents, plans, contracts, specifications, or approved records.
Evidence independently supported by multiple reliable sources.
Evidence provided by credible ecosystem participants or internal experts.
Evidence based primarily on seller observation or interpretation.
Unvalidated assumption that must not be treated as confirmed fact.

conflictResolutionRules: Higher-confidence evidence takes precedence over lower-confidence evidence.
More recent validated evidence may supersede outdated evidence.
Contradictory high-confidence evidence must remain visible as an unresolved contradiction.
The AI must not silently discard material contradictory evidence.
When evidence is insufficient, the AI should explicitly state uncertainty.

reasoningWorkflow.purpose: Define the sequence through which AI reasoning should analyze a pipeline.

steps.name: Establish Pipeline Context
steps.reasoningObjective: Understand the commercial situation, revenue motion, industry context, pipeline stage, deal characteristics, and inherited qualification context.

steps.name: Resolve Configuration Context
steps.reasoningObjective: Apply universal, revenue-motion-specific, and industry-specific intelligence using the defined inheritance precedence.

steps.name: Interpret Evidence
steps.reasoningObjective: Analyze the meaning, quality, strength, confidence, recency, and relevance of available evidence.

steps.name: Synthesize PADF Dimension Conditions
steps.reasoningObjective: Explain why each dimension is strong, weak, uncertain, improving, or deteriorating.

steps.name: Identify Cross-Dimensional Relationships
steps.reasoningObjective: Identify causal relationships, dependencies, contradictions, and reinforcing patterns between dimensions.

steps.name: Diagnose Evidence Gaps
steps.reasoningObjective: Determine which missing or weak evidence materially limits assessment confidence or pipeline progress.

steps.name: Interpret Risk Signals
steps.reasoningObjective: Analyze triggered risks, group related symptoms, identify probable root causes, and distinguish cause from consequence.

steps.name: Evaluate Winability
steps.reasoningObjective: Synthesize positive conditions, negative conditions, uncertainty, risk exposure, and pipeline momentum into an explainable interpretation of winning possibility.

steps.name: Develop Winning Strategy
steps.reasoningObjective: Select the most relevant strategic interventions based on diagnosed root causes and expected winability impact.

steps.name: Prioritize Actions
steps.reasoningObjective: Sequence actions according to urgency, expected impact, feasibility, dependencies, and time remaining.

steps.name: Identify Next Best Action
steps.reasoningObjective: Select the single most important immediate action capable of creating meaningful positive movement.

steps.name: Evaluate Historical Evolution
steps.reasoningObjective: Determine whether the pipeline is strengthening, weakening, stagnating, or recovering over time.

steps.name: Generate Explainable Recommendation
steps.reasoningObjective: Produce a transparent conclusion connecting evidence, diagnosis, risk, strategy, actions, and expected outcomes.

crossDimensionalReasoningModel.purpose: Enable the AI to reason about relationships between PADF dimensions rather than evaluating dimensions independently.

relationshipTypes.description: Weakness in one dimension may cause or contribute to weakness in another.
Multiple strong dimensions reinforce the overall pipeline position.
Multiple weaknesses combine to create a larger risk than their individual scores indicate.
Evidence or assessment conclusions across dimensions are inconsistent.
A weak dimension limits the ability to realize the benefit of another strong dimension.

reasoningExamples.pattern: Strong business need + weak economic buyer access
reasoningExamples.interpretation: The opportunity may have genuine value but insufficient executive sponsorship to secure investment approval.
Internal advocacy exists, but the seller may not understand how to convert support into a formal decision.

reasoningExamples.pattern: High solution fit + low quantified value
reasoningExamples.interpretation: The solution may solve the problem technically but lacks a sufficiently compelling business case.

reasoningExamples.pattern: Strong stakeholder access + deteriorating timeline confidence
reasoningExamples.interpretation: Customer engagement may be positive, but internal customer dependencies or approval constraints are delaying the decision.

reasoningExamples.pattern: Strong value case + weak competitive position
reasoningExamples.interpretation: The opportunity may require reframing, differentiation, or stakeholder strategy rather than additional value discovery.

rootCauseReasoningModel.purpose: Guide the AI to distinguish observable symptoms from probable underlying causes.
rootCauseReasoningPrinciples: Do not assume that the lowest-scoring dimension is automatically the root cause.
Analyze evidence chronology and cross-dimensional relationships.
Identify whether multiple symptoms originate from a common underlying condition.
Represent multiple root-cause hypotheses when evidence is insufficient to identify a single cause.

winabilityReasoningModel.purpose: Define how AI should explain the meaning of calculated or assessed pipeline winability.
interpretationPrinciples: Winability must distinguish between favorable conditions and confidence in those conditions.
A high score with weak evidence confidence must be presented as uncertain.
A moderate score with improving evidence and strong momentum may have a more favorable trajectory than a higher but deteriorating score.
Material critical risks must be visible even when aggregate winability is high.
Winability explanations must identify the most influential positive and negative drivers.

winningStrategyReasoningModel.purpose: Define how the AI selects and adapts winning strategies.
strategySelectionPrinciples: Strategies must address diagnosed root causes rather than generic dimension weaknesses.
Strategies must consider pipeline stage and time remaining.
Strategies must respect revenue motion and industry context.
Strategies should prioritize actions with meaningful expected impact on winability.
Strategies should account for dependencies between actions.
The AI may combine multiple strategy categories when risks are interdependent.
Strategies should be updated when new evidence materially changes the diagnosis.

recommendationGenerationModel.purpose: Define how strategic recommendations are transformed into actionable recommendations.

recommendationLevels.description: Defines the overall approach required to improve the pipeline.
Defines the specific intervention required to execute the strategy.

recommendationGenerationModel.replacementPrinciple: Generic recommendations must be converted into a specific action directed at a specific stakeholder, decision, risk, evidence gap, or progression event.

nextBestActionModel.purpose: Identify the single action with the highest immediate expected value for improving pipeline health or reducing material risk.
selectionPrinciples: The next best action should remove the most important constraint when possible.
The next best action may be an evidence acquisition action when uncertainty is the primary constraint.
The next best action should create measurable progression rather than merely increase activity.
The next best action must have a clear success condition.

actionPrioritizationReasoningModel.purpose: Guide AI prioritization across multiple possible actions.

priorityLevels.meaning: Immediate intervention required to prevent material deterioration or probable loss.
Highest-value strategic action with significant expected impact.

historicalEvolutionReasoningModel.purpose: Enable AI to reason about how the pipeline evolves over time rather than treating every assessment as an isolated snapshot.

trajectoryStates.description: Evidence, dimension health, risk position, and/or momentum are improving.
Pipeline remains healthy without material deterioration.
Pipeline has not materially changed but uncertainty remains unresolved.
Risk exposure, uncertainty, or negative evidence is increasing.
Previously deteriorated conditions are improving following intervention.

historicalReasoningQuestions: What materially changed since the previous assessment?
Which risks are new, worsening, improving, or resolved?
Did completed actions produce the expected evidence or outcome?
Is winability changing because of real customer progress or merely internal optimism?
Are forecast changes supported by evidence?
Which unresolved risks have persisted across multiple assessments?

uncertaintyAndConfidenceModel.purpose: Ensure that AI distinguishes between a negative condition and uncertainty about the condition.

uncertaintyTypes.description: Not enough evidence exists to support a reliable conclusion.
Reliable evidence sources provide contradictory conclusions.
Evidence may no longer represent the current customer situation.
The conclusion depends materially on unvalidated assumptions.
Required commercial or industry context is missing.

uncertaintyAndConfidenceModel.reasoningRule: The AI must not convert uncertainty into a negative or positive fact without explicit evidence.

recommendationImpactModel.purpose: Estimate the expected influence of recommended actions on pipeline health and winability.

impactLevels.description: Action could materially change the overall opportunity position.
Action is expected to significantly reduce a material risk or improve a critical dimension.
Action is expected to improve pipeline position but is unlikely to independently change the outcome.
Action provides incremental improvement or additional validation.

recommendationImpactModel.impactReasoningRule: Expected impact is a hypothesis and must be distinguished from validated realized impact.

explainabilityFramework.purpose: Ensure all material AI conclusions can be understood and challenged by users.

explainabilityRequirements.description: Material conclusions should reference the evidence or evidence conditions supporting them.
The output should explain the logical relationship between evidence, diagnosis, and conclusion.
Recommended strategies should identify the risks or root causes they address.
Actions should explain why they are prioritized.
Material uncertainty and missing evidence must remain visible.
When historical comparisons are used, the output should identify what changed.

aiReasoningGuardrails.purpose: Prevent unsupported, generic, inconsistent, or unsafe reasoning behavior.

guardrails.name: No Evidence Fabrication
guardrails.rule: The AI must not invent customer facts, stakeholder positions, competitive information, or pipeline events.

guardrails.name: Assumption Labeling
guardrails.rule: Unvalidated assumptions must be explicitly represented as assumptions.

guardrails.name: Configuration Respect
guardrails.rule: The AI must use the resolved universal, revenue motion, and industry configuration context.

guardrails.name: Evidence Before Conclusion
guardrails.rule: Material conclusions must be supported by evidence, deterministic signals, or explicitly labeled hypotheses.

guardrails.name: Root Cause Before Recommendation
guardrails.rule: Recommendations should address diagnosed causes or clearly stated hypotheses rather than only symptoms.

guardrails.name: No Generic Advice
guardrails.rule: Recommendations must be contextualized to the pipeline condition.

guardrails.name: Confidence Transparency
guardrails.rule: Low-confidence conclusions must not be presented as certain.

guardrails.name: Contradiction Visibility
guardrails.rule: Material contradictory evidence must be surfaced.

guardrails.name: Human Decision Authority
guardrails.rule: AI recommendations support human commercial judgment and do not autonomously commit commercial actions.

guardrails.name: Historical Integrity
guardrails.rule: Historical snapshots must remain immutable after creation, while later assessments may reference them.

aiRecommendationOutputModel.purpose: Define the normalized AI reasoning and recommendation output.

executiveReasoningSummaryModel.purpose: Generate a concise executive-level interpretation without losing evidence-based integrity.

What is working in our favor?
What could cause us to lose?

What has changed since the previous assessment?

rules.name: ContextFirst
rules.description: Establish revenue motion, industry, stage, and pipeline context before interpreting evidence.

rules.name: ConfigurationInheritance
rules.description: Resolve configuration using Industry Override > Revenue Motion Override > Universal Baseline.

rules.name: EvidenceWeightedReasoning
rules.description: Prioritize validated, authoritative, recent, and corroborated evidence.

rules.name: SymptomCauseSeparation
rules.description: Separate observed pipeline symptoms from probable root causes.

rules.name: CrossDimensionSynthesis
rules.description: Evaluate interactions between PADF dimensions when they materially affect interpretation.

rules.name: RiskAwareWinability
rules.description: Interpret winability in the context of both aggregate health and unresolved material risks.

rules.name: StrategyRootCauseAlignment
rules.description: Map strategies to root causes and risks rather than only low-scoring dimensions.

rules.name: ActionSpecificity
rules.description: Recommended actions must specify what should happen, why, and what evidence would demonstrate success.

rules.name: TimeAwarePrioritization
rules.description: Action priority must consider pipeline stage and available time before the expected decision.

rules.name: HistoricalComparison
rules.description: Where historical data exists, identify material changes and distinguish actual progression from unchanged optimism.

rules.name: UncertaintyDisclosure
rules.description: Explicitly disclose material evidence gaps, assumptions, contradictions, and low-confidence conclusions.

rules.name: ExplainableOutput
rules.description: Every material conclusion should provide a concise evidence-based rationale.

pipelineEvidenceKnowledgeBaseReleaseMeta.changeSummary: Adds governed evidence-to-SWOT mappings, explicit identifier compatibility, context resolution, evidence validation, TOWS integration, and an adapter to the existing Phase 7 Winning Strategy engine.

integrationMetadata.componentName: Pipeline Evidence Knowledge Base SWOT Integration
integrationMetadata.approvalBasis: User approved the reviewed Evidence-to-SWOT mapping audit in this conversation.
integrationMetadata.purpose: Provide a governed, traceable, context-aware bridge from the reusable 48-object Pipeline Evidence Knowledge Base to the 96 configured SWOT factors, TOWS synthesis, and the existing Winning Strategy engine.
integrationMetadata.architectureBoundary: Additive root-level integration. The eight existing KB phases remain unchanged. SWOT factor definitions and context configurations remain owned by Industry Configuration v1.1; this component owns evidence-object-to-factor mappings and runtime integration contracts.

compatibilityRules: Preserve legacy identifiers in frozen KB phases 4 and 5.
Resolve legacy identifiers through this explicit registry; do not infer aliases by array position or ordinal sequence.
Use canonical revenue-motion and industry identifiers when joining to Industry Configuration v1.1.
Preserve both source and canonical identifiers in runtime traceability records.

mappingStrengthDefinitions.DIRECT: Evidence object is directly relevant to the configured factor's evidence expectations and aligned PADF role.
mappingStrengthDefinitions.SUPPORTING: Evidence object can corroborate or enrich factor evaluation but should not independently establish the factor.
mappingStrengthDefinitions.INDIRECT: Evidence object is contextually or secondarily relevant; apply only with explicit runtime reasoning and additional corroboration where needed.

mappingResolutionRules: A mapping establishes eligibility and relevance, not the truth of a factor.
An evidence object may map to multiple factors and a factor may receive evidence from multiple objects.
Do not assume every evidence object must map to every factor.
Do not interpret mapping strength as evidence quality, evidence confidence, or factor polarity.
Only evaluate mappings for factors active in the resolved universal plus revenue-motion plus industry context.
The actual opportunity evidence instance determines relationship type, polarity, recency, quality, and confidence.

validationSequence: Resolve the active SWOT factor set from Industry Configuration v1.1.
Retrieve evidence instances linked to each eligible reusable evidence object.
Check evidence relevance against the factor's configured evidence expectations and analytical criteria.
Validate source, ownership, customer confirmation, specificity, recency, and consistency.
Determine runtime relationship type and polarity from the evidence instance.
Assess whether evidence is sufficient, partial, contradictory, stale, or missing.
Retain traceability from factor conclusion to evidence instance, evidence object, mapping, PADF dimension, and source.

polarityGovernance.principle: A reusable evidence object has no fixed positive or negative polarity.
polarityGovernance.prohibition: Never assign a factor as strength, weakness, opportunity, or threat solely because an evidence object is mapped to it.

mappingStrengthUse.DIRECT: Eligible as primary evidence subject to evidence quality and factor criteria.
mappingStrengthUse.SUPPORTING: Use as corroborating evidence; do not treat as sufficient alone unless factor criteria explicitly permit.
mappingStrengthUse.INDIRECT: Use as contextual signal only; require explicit reasoning and corroboration.

contextResolutionPrinciples: Universal mappings are eligible across all supported contexts.
Revenue-motion mappings are eligible only when their canonical revenue-motion context is active.
Industry mappings are eligible only when their canonical industry context is active.
Industry and revenue-motion context are resolved independently using canonical identifiers.
Do not activate all 96 factors for a single opportunity; activate the applicable 8 universal, 4 revenue-motion, and 4 industry factors where the configuration defines that pattern.

responsibilitySplit.industryConfiguration: Owns SWOT taxonomy, factor definitions, context-specific factor criteria, evidence expectations, and factor evaluation governance.
responsibilitySplit.evidenceKnowledgeBase: Owns reusable evidence object definitions and this evidence-to-factor mapping catalogue.
responsibilitySplit.runtimeAssessment: Owns actual opportunity evidence instances, validation outcomes, factor polarity, factor assessment, and evidence traceability.

assessmentConstraints: Do not create a SWOT finding without opportunity-specific evidence or an explicitly labeled evidence gap.
Do not use industry characteristics as proof of an opportunity-specific factor.
Separate observed facts, customer-confirmed statements, seller assumptions, and AI inferences.
Retain negative and contradictory evidence rather than suppressing it.
Use configured factor criteria and evidence expectations; mapping alone is insufficient.

combinationDefinitions.SO: Use substantiated strengths to capture evidence-supported opportunities.
combinationDefinitions.WO: Address substantiated weaknesses to unlock evidence-supported opportunities.
combinationDefinitions.ST: Use substantiated strengths to mitigate or respond to evidence-supported threats.
combinationDefinitions.WT: Reduce substantiated weaknesses and exposure to evidence-supported threats.

combinationEligibilityRules: Both contributing SWOT findings must be active, sufficiently evidenced, and traceable.
The combination must have a clear causal or strategic relationship, not merely share keywords.
Do not generate a TOWS strategy from an unmapped or unsupported factor.
Retain contributing factor IDs, evidence object IDs, evidence instance IDs, mapping IDs, and rationale.
Do not duplicate equivalent combinations or strategies.
Apply configured TOWS prioritization and evaluation rules from Industry Configuration v1.1.

rules: Use the existing Phase 7 risk triggers and winning-strategy categories; do not create a parallel risk or strategy engine.
Use TOWS outputs as evidence-backed strategic inputs to the existing Phase 7 recommendation process.
Preserve existing Phase 7 strategy category identifiers, risk trigger identifiers, action fields, and status lifecycle.
A TOWS recommendation must be mapped to an existing Phase 7 category before it is emitted as a winning-strategy recommendation.
Risk signals may qualify or constrain a TOWS recommendation and must remain traceable to their source evidence.

mandatoryReasoningBehaviors: Distinguish reusable evidence definitions from actual opportunity evidence instances.
Use mapping strength as relevance guidance, not as a confidence score.
Determine runtime relationship and polarity from the actual evidence instance.
Identify evidence gaps and contradictory evidence explicitly.
Do not fabricate evidence, customer confirmation, or source details.
Explain why evidence supports, contradicts, qualifies, contextualizes, signals a gap, or indicates change.
Maintain end-to-end traceability through SWOT, TOWS, risk, and winning-strategy outputs.
